plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate leveraged ETF exposure. Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet mandate. Add to QQQI for increased income and stability. Buy MSFT as a top-quality name for diversification. Trim CRWD to reduce single name concentration.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets capital preservation with a potential return of ~1.5%/month. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration, but also limits upside potential.

plan: Trim SOXL and SPAL to reduce leveraged ETF exposure. Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet mandate. Buy NVDA as a strong scanner setup for growth. Trim CRWD to reduce single name concentration. Buy MSFT as a quality tech name for diversification.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for risk-first growth, targeting ~2.5%/month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index exposure with quality tech, accepting moderate risk for growth potential.

plan: Add to SOXL and SPAL to increase leveraged ETF exposure. Trim SPY to 25% to meet mandate and reallocate. Buy NVDA, concentrating in a highest-scoring setup. Buy CRCL, adding a high R-factor scanner setup. Add to SMH to increase semiconductor exposure.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets stretch growth, aiming for ~4%/month. It leans into leverage and concentration in high-scoring setups, which significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk. Leveraged ETFs decay daily, and strict stop discipline is crucial to manage potential rapid losses.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate leveraged ETFs. Add to QQQI to prioritize income and distributions. Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet mandate. Trim QQQ to reduce growth exposure. Buy MSFT as a quality name for stability.
income.read: This income plan focuses on parking cash for yield, targeting ~1%/month. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income through income/covered-call ETFs and broad index exposure. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in a selloff, so it is not a savings account.
